Europe (EU broadly; UK specifically mentioned; Slovakia, Austria, Hungary cited)

**Temporal focus:**
T1. Historical observation — YES
T2. Forward-looking immediate — YES
T3. Long-term development — YES

**Synopsis:**
S&P warns that intensifying European heatwaves are creating mounting financial pressure on life, health, and re/insurers via surging heat-related mortality and hospitalisation claims. Europe's rapidly ageing population amplifies vulnerability, with ~9,000 of ~10,650 excess deaths during one June heatwave occurring in the 65+ cohort. Near-term ratings impact is contained, but S&P flags medium-to-long-term downgrade risk as heatwaves grow more frequent and severe. The financial feedback loop is expected to drive premium increases for consumers.
